The following meeting was held in a hybrid format that allowed members of the public to
participate in—person and remotely Via Zoom when technically Viable.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Peak called the meeting to order at 6:31 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Skylar Peak and Commissioners Drew Leonard, John G. Mazza and
  Elizabeth Riddick

  ABSENT: Vice Chair Marni Kamins

  ALSO PRESENT: Tyler Eaton, Assistant Community Development Director; Trevor

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Paul Allen Brown alleged there was a conflict ol‘ interest regarding Commissioner
  Mazza’s position as a Commissioner on the Planning Commission and his position
  as Vice Chair on the Malibu Township Council. He added that Commissioner
  Mazza had served 16 years on the Planning Commission and should retire from his
  role.

  Sterling Paige was called on to give comment and provided only a greeting to the
  Commission.

  Commissioner Mazza addressed Paul Allen Brown’s comment and explained that
  recusals were how Commissioners dealt with conflicts of interest.

  Chair Peak expressed his hope that everyone was having a wonderful summer.

  Commissioner Mazza encouraged the public to attend the Public Works
  Commission meeting on July 22. 2026 and provide comment on the community
  lands project. He expressed the importance of public input on future uses of the
  City-owned vacant parcels.

  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR REPORT

  Assistant Community Development Director Eaton thanked Commissioner Mazza
  for reminding the public about the community lands proj ect and announced that the
  project would be heard at both the Parks and Recreation and Public Works
  Commission meetings. He announced that Community Development Director
  Bundy would be available at the Rebuild Center Monday through Friday for the
  foreseeable future and mentioned that an appointment was highly recommended.
  He explained that Phase l of the wireless residential fix was approved by the City
  Council on July l3, 2026 and that Phase 2 was scheduled for the August 24, 2026
  Regular City Council Meeting. He also noted that the Local Coastal Program
  Amendment to create a definition for beachfront was scheduled for the August 10,
  2026 Regular City Council meeting. Mr. Eaton announced the Community
  Development Department would present to the Zoning Ordinance Revisions and
  Code Enforcement Subcommittee in the next few months to create a policy on
  blufftop determinations and biology inspections.
   Malibu Planning Commission

  Page 3 0f 10

  Associate Planner Elias provided an update regarding rebuild statistics and
  upcoming rebuild meetings.

  Commissioner Leonard asked staff how many permits had been issued on
  beachfront homes.

  In response to Commissioner Leonard, Associate Planner Elias explained that there
  had been ten building plan check permits issued for beachfront homes to date.

  Commissioner Leonard asked staff how many Palisades Fire rebuild properties
  were under active construction.

  In response to Commissioner Leonard, Assistant Community Development
  Director Eaton noted that he was aware ofa few Palisades Fire rebuilds under active
  construction.

  Commissioner Mazza asked staff if they had any information regarding a K—rail
  that was recently installed on Pacific Coast Highway and questioned ifevacuation
  studies were done to evaluate the safety of having one lane in that area.

  In response to Commissioner Mazza, Assistant Community Development Director
  Eaton explained that Public Works usually took the lead on PCH projects and that
  he would return with information on the K—rail at the next Planning Commission
  meeting after speaking with Public Works staff.

  Chair Peak commented that he believed the K-rail was temporarily installed to
  improve worker safety.
